findings.claim: classify_credit_score (demo-repo/src/loanflow/risk_bands.py:45-54) does not check the type of score. Its first statement is the range check `if not (300 <= score <= 850): raise ValidationError(...)`, followed by bucket thresholds <580 POOR, <670 FAIR, <740 GOOD, else EXCELLENT. So a float such as 700.5 passes the range check and returns CreditBucket.GOOD. Because bool is an int subclass, True/False (1/0) are rejected today only by the range check, not by a type check.

ValidationError is already imported in risk_bands.py from loanflow.errors, so no new import is needed. ValidationError is defined in demo-repo/src/loanflow/errors.py:14 as a subclass of LoanflowError.

Money.__post_init__ uses the integer-validation convention `if isinstance(self.cents, bool) or not isinstance(self.cents, int): raise ValidationError("Money.cents must be an integer number of cents")` at primitives.py:24-25. Percentage.__post_init__ uses the same form for basis_points at primitives.py:54-55, and this type check runs before its separate negative-value check at primitives.py:56-57.

test_risk_bands.py imports pytest, ValidationError, and classify_credit_score (lines 3-6). The existing rejection test, test_credit_score_out_of_range_is_rejected (lines 47-51), takes no fixtures, is annotated `-> None`, and uses one `with pytest.raises(ValidationError):` block per bad input (299, 851). test_credit_bucket_boundaries (lines 37-44) asserts the 579/580/669/670/739/740 boundaries with `is` identity checks.

A sibling regression test with the same convention already exists for Percentage: test_percentage_rejects_non_integer_and_bool_basis_points (demo-repo/tests/unit/test_primitives.py:47-53). It uses separate pytest.raises(ValidationError) blocks for 1.5, True and False, each marked `# type: ignore[arg-type]`.

The only production call site of classify_credit_score is risk_profile.py:48 inside build_risk_profile, whose credit_score parameter is annotated int (line 41). The CLI path converts its input with `int(payload["credit_score"])` at cli.py:45 before passing it on. Every test call site found passes integer literals (for example 780, 600, 560, 500).
No in-repo caller or test passes a float or bool credit score to classify_credit_score or build_risk_profile.

findings.claim: Adding the type check to classify_credit_score should not break any existing in-repo caller or test. Because the check runs before the range check, integer boundary behaviour (579/580/669/670/739/740) and the 299/851 rejections stay the same.
findings.reasoning: F-6 shows every caller and test supplies an int (or an int()-converted value). A plain int fails neither isinstance(score, bool) nor `not isinstance(score, int)`, so ints reach the unchanged range and threshold logic in F-1. The existing tests in F-4 pass only ints, so their results should not change.
